api/Fizzy.McapSharp.html.summary: Namespace Fizzy.McapSharp Classes McapAsyncMessageReader Incremental asynchronous resolved message reader. Owns its Stream unless leaveOpen is true. Allows one outstanding operation, which must be consumed exactly once. Expanded reads validate record bodies and declaration references independently of CRC options. McapAsyncRecordReader Incremental asynchronous record reader. Owns its Stream unless leaveOpen is true. Allows one outstanding operation, which must be consumed exactly once. Expanded reads validate record bodies and declaration references independently of CRC options. McapAttachment Owned attachment payload and fields. Times use caller-defined nanoseconds. McapAttachmentHeader Attachment fields. LogTime and CreateTime use caller-defined nanoseconds. McapAttachmentIndex Owned attachment index with byte Offset from the MCAP origin (the initial Stream position for Stream inputs) and record Length; DataSize counts payload bytes and times are nanoseconds. McapAttachmentRecord Owned attachment body and stored CRC. McapBatchWriteException A failed batch may have written a prefix and part of its failing record. McapChannel Resolved channel declaration with optional schema and metadata. Reader results own their data; direct construction retains supplied references. McapChannelDescription Immutable resolved channel declaration shareable across messages and threads; survives reader disposal. McapChannelRecord Owned channel record retaining the schema ID rather than resolving the schema object. McapChunkFlattener Expanded file records with record-body and declaration-reference validation independent of CRC options. McapChunkHeader Chunk descriptor. Times are nanoseconds; sizes are bytes; UncompressedCrc covers expanded record bytes. McapChunkIndex Owned chunk index. ChunkStartOffset and MessageIndexOffsets are byte offsets from the MCAP origin (the initial Stream position for Stream inputs); lengths and sizes are bytes; times are nanoseconds. McapChunkReader Records from one encoded Chunk body, without its outer record header. Validation is local to the chunk; declarations may live elsewhere. McapChunkRecord Owned chunk record. Data contains the compressed bytes described by Header. McapException A structured MCAP failure. Reader sessions normally become terminal; writer continuation is limited to CanContinueWriting. McapFormat Constants identifying the MCAP wire format and bundled upstream implementation. McapHeader Owned file header containing the profile and writer library identifier. McapIndexedQuery Indexed message selection. Omitted and empty queries use ascending log time. Requires complete indexes and never falls back to scanning or buffered sorting. McapIndexedReader Owns copied or explicitly mapped input and its official summary, independently of the originating session. Indexed-reader message callbacks must not invoke operations on any indexed reader or prepared chunk index, including disposal. McapIndexedReaderOptions Limits only the indexed reader cache, not upstream allocations or live leases. McapLinearReader Top-level records; chunk bodies remain encoded. Does not validate declarations hidden inside chunks. McapMessage Message with resolved declarations and payload bytes. Reader results own independent data; direct construction retains supplied references. Times use caller-defined nanoseconds. McapMessageBatchLease Owns stable native message storage. Keep this lease alive until all payload access has finished. Access and disposal must not overlap. Payload spans expire on disposal. A payload slice can retain an entire chunk, copied input or mapping; payload length is not retained capacity. McapMessageFilter Selects messages during a sequential file-order scan. Omitted and empty filters are equivalent; filtering never selects indexes or requests sorting. McapMessageIndex Owned per-channel message index, including channels with an empty Records collection. McapMessageLease An independently retained message. Do not dispose concurrently with payload access. McapMessageReader Resolved messages with declaration-reference validation. Results follow the selected caller-buffer, borrowing or retained-storage ownership contract. McapMessageRecord Owned message record with an independent payload array. McapMetadata Owned named string metadata record. McapMetadataIndex Owned metadata index with byte Offset from the MCAP origin (the initial Stream position for Stream inputs) and complete record Length in bytes. McapPreparedAttachment Copies attachment fields. The payload is supplied separately at each write. Preparation does not write or register anything. McapPreparedAttachmentStart Copies segmented attachment fields and the exact declared byte length. Preparation does not write or register anything. McapPreparedChannel An immutable native snapshot. Preparing does not register or write declarations. McapPreparedChannelRegistration Copies a channel registration descriptor referring to a schema ID. This is distinct from a resolved prepared channel. Preparation does not write or register anything. McapPreparedChunkIndex An immutable, native-owned copy of a Chunk index for repeated operations across indexed readers. McapPreparedMetadata Copies named metadata for repeated synchronous writes. Preparation does not write or register anything. McapPreparedSchema Copies schema fields and bytes for repeated registration. Null ID requests allocation; explicit ID must be nonzero. Preparation does not write or register anything. McapQuery Message selection with inclusive StartTime and exclusive EndTime. Topic and Topics are mutually exclusive. Explicit query execution defaults to ascending log time for both omitted and empty queries. Use McapMessageFilter for sequential file-order selection. McapRawMessageReader Raw message headers and payloads. Encountered declarations are collected, but a message need not reference a known channel. No implicit resolved-message enumeration is provided. Results follow the selected caller-buffer, borrowing or retained-storage ownership contract. McapRawRecord An independently owned opcode and unparsed record body. Data excludes the opcode and length prefix. Use McapRecords.Parse for typed fields. McapReaderFactory Reusable reader factory with instance methods for a file path and static methods for Streams; construction validates the path but does not open the file. This factory owns no disposable resources. Each opened session or enumeration owns an independent native reader and its input. McapReaderOptions Parsing and integrity options for one read session. Defaults do not prove full-file integrity; a strict complete expanded synchronous scan provides full-file validation. High-level body and declaration checks do not depend on this preset. McapRecordAccessor Serialized random access over one seekable file or Stream, without copying the complete input. Offsets are relative to the initial MCAP position. Parsing or I/O failure terminates this reader; independent copied indexed readers survive disposal. McapRecords Parses record bodies into independent owned models and exposes MCAP layout helpers. McapRecoveryResult Result of explicit prefix salvage. IsFullyValidated is true only after a strict complete scan; Error describes the failure that ended salvage, if any. McapSansIoIndexedReader Caller-driven indexed parser. Performs no I/O. Supply requested input before advancing again; buffer-size negotiation preserves pending delivery and other protocol failures are terminal. McapSansIoLinearReader Caller-driven linear parser. Performs no I/O. Supply requested input before advancing again; buffer-size negotiation preserves pending delivery and other protocol failures are terminal. McapSansIoSummaryReader Caller-driven summary parser. Performs no I/O. Supply requested input or acknowledge the requested seek before advancing again; protocol failures are terminal. McapSchema Schema declaration. Reader results own independent mutable schema bytes; direct construction retains the supplied array. McapSchemaDescription An immutable declaration snapshot that can be shared across messages and threads. McapStatistics Owned summary statistics. Message times are nanoseconds; counts describe the recorded data section. McapSummary Summary model. Library-returned snapshots own independent collections; direct construction retains supplied references. Contains complete schema/channel declarations, with shared schema references inside one result. Separate results are independent. Arrays and collections retain ordinary .NET equality semantics. Size grows with file indexes and declarations. McapSummaryReaderOptions Options for direct Sans-I/O summary reading. FileSize permits end-relative seeks to be resolved against the caller-provided source length. McapSummaryRecordReader Retained summary records. The reader survives disposal of its originating writer, snapshot or summary parser; it does not scan file contents. McapWriter A serialized MCAP writer. Complete explicitly to finish the format; disposal only releases resources. Native or I/O failures are terminal except for configured audited pre-mutation rejections. McapWriterOptions Writer configuration fixed at construction. Null emission/CRC switches retain upstream settings; other nullable settings have the semantics documented on their properties. Input payloads are consumed synchronously; Complete must be called explicitly. Structs McapBatchReadResult A successful batch result. Count identifies valid header/range entries and BytesWritten the valid payload prefix. On BufferTooSmall, RequiredLength is the entire pending message payload size; retry preserves that message. No result is published on exception. McapCacheStatistics Cumulative snapshot diagnostics: Hits counts cache reuse and ChunkLoads counts actual chunk loads, including loads not retained by the cache. Not allocation or memory statistics. McapDataEnd Data-section end marker containing its stored CRC. McapFooter Footer fields: summary offsets are byte positions from the MCAP origin (the initial Stream position for Stream inputs); SummaryCrc is the stored summary checksum. McapIndexedReadEvent An indexed protocol event. ReadChunk uses Length and Offset for compressed data excluding the Chunk header, relative to the MCAP origin. Message uses Length and Header. McapLinearReadEvent A linear protocol event. Length is in bytes; Opcode applies only to Record events. McapMessageHeader Message descriptor. LogTime and PublishTime are caller-defined nanoseconds; ChannelId refers to a declared channel. McapMessageIndexEntry Message log time in nanoseconds and byte offset within the uncompressed chunk record stream, not an offset from the MCAP origin. McapMessageSeekRequest One random message lookup. Index must remain undisposed during the call; Entry.Offset is relative to expanded chunk bytes. McapPayloadRange Byte offset and length within the payload storage passed to the same batch operation; not a file offset. McapRecordFields Allocation-free typed field cursor. Length-prefixed collections can be traversed with another cursor. McapRecordReadResult Caller-buffer read outcome. On Success, Opcode identifies the record and Length is the body bytes copied; on BufferTooSmall, Length is the required capacity and the same record remains pending. EOF does not prove full-file integrity. McapRecordView A record body validated at Parse time over caller-owned memory. Keep the underlying bytes unchanged for the entire lifetime of this view and all derived field cursors or spans. Read-only spans do not prevent mutation through other aliases. UTF-8 and collection fields remain borrowed spans; ToOwned creates an independent copy. McapSeekRequest A requested source position. Begin uses an unsigned absolute position; Current and End use a signed relative offset. Positions are relative to the MCAP origin. McapSummaryOffset Summary group descriptor with byte start from the MCAP origin (the initial Stream position for Stream inputs) and byte length. McapSummaryReadEvent A summary protocol event. Length applies to Read; Seek applies to Seek. Positions are relative to the MCAP origin. Other fields are not meaningful. McapVisitResult Number of completed visitor calls and why traversal stopped. VisitorStopped includes the message whose callback returned false; callback exceptions publish no result. Interfaces IMcapRecord A record model. Results returned by Parse(byte, ReadOnlySpan<byte>) are independently owned. Pattern match the concrete record type to access its fields. Unknown opcodes return McapRawRecord; no payload or collection borrows the input span. Enums McapBatchStopReason Why a successful batch read or visit stopped; errors throw instead of returning this status. McapCompression Compression codec used for chunks; None leaves record bytes uncompressed. McapErrorKind Structured MCAP or binding failure classification. Consult Details for kind-specific native fields; this is not a retry policy. McapIndexedEventKind Events produced by the indexed protocol. McapLinearEventKind Events produced by the linear protocol. McapOpcode Standard MCAP record opcodes. Private records use byte values 0x80-0xFF. McapReadOrder Message traversal ordering; equal log-time ordering is unspecified. McapReadStatus Outcome of a caller-buffer read or Sans-I/O event poll. Success describes availability, not a particular MCAP opcode. McapSummaryEventKind Events produced by the summary protocol. McapValidationCapability Creation-time validation scope, independent of current progress, failure or disposal. McapWriterSafeRejections Audited pre-mutation native rejections that may leave the writer usable. I/O and cleanup failures remain terminal. Delegates McapMessageVisitor Consumes a borrowed payload synchronously. Return false to stop after this message. The span expires on return. Do not call back into the originating reader.

docs/api.html.title: API, lifetime, and data ownership | Fizzy.McapSharp
docs/api.html.summary: API, lifetime, and data ownership English | 简体中文 This is the cross-API contract reference for defaults, ownership, failure and validation boundaries. Start with the tutorial for first use; consult queries, message ownership, Streams and async or Sans-I/O for task-oriented guidance. Read by responsibility: capability selection → writing → reading and queries → lifetime and errors → validation and recovery → performance guarantees. Fizzy.McapSharp provides MCAP file, Stream, buffer and Sans-I/O operations on .NET 8: Windows x64 and glibc Linux x64/ARM64, built against Ubuntu 22.04. macOS, musl and 32-bit processes are unsupported. Applications define payload encodings and nanosecond clock semantics. Cancellable asynchronous record reading and time sorting are available; payload decoding remains application-defined. See the official API coverage map. Read/write capabilities Find the capability first, then choose input/output, delivery ownership and access pattern. These are library capabilities; their relationship to official Rust APIs is documented in the coverage map. Capability Writing paths Reading paths Messages Header + span, complete message, prepared channel, batch and lease forwarding Owned enumeration, caller buffer, borrowed callback, batch lease Schemas and channels Explicit registration or automatic declarations with complete messages Encountered declaration lookup, immutable descriptions, owned enumeration Metadata WriteMetadata, prepared operation Enumeration or indexed ReadMetadata Attachments Whole payload, prepared operation, segmented attachment Enumeration or indexed ReadAttachment Raw records WritePrivateRecord for private opcodes Top-level/expanded records, caller buffer, owned records and record views Summary and indexes Writer options control generation; Complete then summary access Summary snapshot/cursor, indexed queries, chunk cursors and random seek Reading arbitrary records does not imply a generic arbitrary-record writer. Writing uses a file or Stream; reading also offers copied/mapped buffers and direct Sans-I/O. See writing details, owned/raw reading and reader adapters. Choose a writing path All payload inputs are consumed synchronously. Choose based on how declarations and payload storage are already represented; batching reduces call overhead but is not atomic. Path Declarations and preparation Suitable use WriteToKnownChannel(in header, span) Register the channel first; warmed path allocates 0 B managed Repeated messages on known channels, reusable payload buffers WriteMessage(McapMessage) Observes current descriptions and invokes automatic declarations; convenience work may allocate Writing existing owned message objects Prepared-channel WriteMessage Prepare an immutable description once; automatic declarations at writing; warmed writes allocate 0 B managed Repeated full-message writes without repeated description serialization WriteBatch(headers, storage, ranges) Register channels first; caller supplies contiguous payload storage and ranges Payloads already share one storage region; avoid repacking solely to batch WriteBatch(lease[, headers]) Register destination channels; optionally replace headers; shares retained payloads across owners Forwarding a read batch without concatenating payloads Preparation may allocate. Typed prepared descriptors similarly reuse schema/channel/metadata/attachment control descriptions. Native writer, codec and Stream costs still apply. Detailed contracts: prepared writes, batch forwarding. Choose message ownership Start with ReadMessages() and independently owned results for ordinary application code. Choose delivery ownership before tuning allocations. A message session applies its query and ordering independently of the delivery method; the methods below expose the selected messages with different result forms and lifetimes. Need API Managed allocation and payload delivery Lifetime Independent, mutable results ReadMessages() Allocates result objects and final payload arrays; copies mutable schema bytes and metadata for each result Independent of the reader Reuse caller storage ReadNext(buffer, ...), ReadBatch(...) Warmed library path allocates 0 B managed; copies payload into caller buffers Caller owns buffers and decides when to overwrite them Process synchronously ReadNext(visitor), VisitMessages(...) Warmed library path allocates 0 B managed; no final payload delivery copy Span expires when the callback returns; no reader reentry Retain across operations or forward ReadBatchLease(...) Allocates lease control objects; shares payload backing without batch repacking Keep the lease alive throughout access; never dispose concurrently All four forms are available on McapMessageReader, including snapshot chunk-message readers. McapRawMessageReader supports buffers, callbacks, batches and leases without resolving every message channel; it deliberately has no owned resolved-message enumeration. McapAsyncMessageReader provides ReadBatchLeaseAsync; McapAsyncRecordReader provides caller-buffer record delivery. Sans-I/O readers expose protocol-specific caller-buffer events. Snapshot random access has its own delivery overloads. ReadMessages() copies to provide independent mutable results, not because message reading requires owned arrays. Buffer and borrowed paths return headers; retrieve declarations separately when needed. Shared immutable declarations are available through GetChannelDescription. Choosing a delivery method does not remove parser input, decompression, query sorting or index costs. See allocation guarantees. Long-lived leases and individual random seeks are valid uses. The retention guidance and access patterns describe performance choices; the lifetime and concurrency rules are correctness requirements. Choose an access pattern Access selects where and in what order to read; delivery ownership selects how results are handed to the caller. They are separate choices, not competing API families. Available combinations depend on the reader. Need Path Main tradeoff Process a recording in file order Sequential message/record session Incremental input; no global result collection for sorting Filter by topic/time in time order Query with usable indexes May buffer overlapping chunks; fallback can collect all matches when indexes are insufficient Reject global buffered sorting QueryMessages with AllowBufferedSort = false Still permits file-order scans and supported indexed queries Require indexes OpenIndexedMessages Fails instead of falling back to a sequential scan or global sort Read many messages in one chunk One OpenChunkMessages cursor Reuses traversal within that cursor Fetch a known set of discrete messages SeekMessages Groups chunk loads within one call; returns a shared batch Revisit chunks across calls Reuse an indexed reader with a cache allowance Trades retained storage for fewer repeated loads/decompressions See query selection, random access and local allowances. The following sections define the operations and their lifetime, failure and validation contracts. Random-access source and storage selection Need Entry Input ownership and cost Read raw records/chunks at known offsets factory.OpenRecordAccessor() or the Stream overload Retains a seekable source; preserves source position for random operations; no complete-input copy Indexed access independent of caller bytes McapIndexedReader.CreateCopied(bytes, options) Copies the complete MCAP input; dispose the returned reader Indexed access independent of a file/Stream factory.CreateCopiedIndexedReader() or the Stream/accessor overload Copies the complete MCAP region; Stream origin is its initial position; copying preserves the accessor position Indexed access without copying the complete file McapIndexedReader.OpenMapped(path, options) Retains a mapping; keep the source unchanged until every dependent cursor and lease is released McapRecordAccessor reads raw records and indexes. McapIndexedReader owns input and provides message seeks, chunk cursors and indexed attachment/metadata reads; it is not merely an index collection. Both require disposal. Stream factory overloads own the source unless leaveOpen: true; the copied reader is independent after creation. SeekMessage does not reposition other cursors. Preparation and cache controls do not change input ownership. Write a recording File creation semantics: McapWriter(path, options) atomically creates a new file and fails if the path already exists, leaving the existing file unchanged. This is the path overload's default protection against accidental overwrites, not a requirement of the MCAP format. McapWriter(stream, options, leaveOpen: false) accepts writable seekable or non-seekable streams. The caller chooses creation or truncation when opening the stream. To explicitly overwrite a file, open a FileStream with FileMode.Create and FileAccess.Write, then pass it to the writer; opening that stream immediately truncates any existing file. A seekable output must be positioned at its end; its current position becomes MCAP offset zero. Non-seekable output uses native chunk buffering. using Fizzy.McapSharp; using var writer = new McapWriter(path, new() { Compression = McapCompression.Zstd }); var schema = writer.RegisterSchema("sample", "jsonschema", "{}"u8); var channel = writer.RegisterChannel("/sample", "json", schema); var header = new McapMessageHeader(channel, Sequence: 0, LogTime: 1000, PublishTime: 900); writer.WriteToKnownChannel(in header, "{\"value\":42}"u8); writer.Complete(); Operation Contract RegisterSchema(name, encoding, data) Returns a native-allocated ushort ID; overload with leading id requests an explicit nonzero ID. Equivalent content can deduplicate. RegisterChannel(topic, messageEncoding, schemaId, metadata) Returns a channel ID; overload with leading id supports explicit IDs, including zero. Schema ID zero means no schema. Conflicting content for an existing ID fails. WriteToKnownChannel(in header, data) Writes to a registered channel using a message header and payload span. Consumes the input synchronously without a managed payload copy. WriteMetadata(name, metadata) Writes string key/value metadata. WriteAttachment(name, mediaType, logTime, createTime, data) Writes one attachment. StartAttachment(..., length), WriteAttachmentBytes(data), FinishAttachment() Writes an attachment in parts with an exact declared length. Other writer operations are rejected until completion. Length mismatch is terminal. WritePrivateRecord(opcode, data, includeInChunks) Accepts opcodes 0x80–0xFF; optionally writes inside chunks. Flush() Flushes the upstream writer, without completing the MCAP footer or guaranteeing durable storage. Complete() Finishes MCAP and flushes output buffers without requesting file persistence. Repeated successful calls are no-ops; the output remains owned until disposal or Stream transfer. FlushToDisk() After successful Complete, requests file persistence for path outputs or directly supplied FileStream; other Streams throw NotSupportedException. GetSummary() Copies the upstream finish result after successful Complete; may allocate. Dispose() Releases resources without implicit Complete. Writer calls are serialized. Applications determine cross-thread business ordering. Native failures outside the configured safe-rejection whitelist and all Stream callback failures make the writer terminal: dispose it and begin a new recording. Argument/state checks before native operations do not by themselves fail a writer. Required strings, dictionaries and owned payload arrays are checked before native writing; null metadata on channel registration means an empty map. Metadata keys and values must be non-null. Input buffers can be reused immediately after return. Completion and file persistence Complete the format, then optionally request operating-system file synchronization: using var writer = new McapWriter(path); // Register channels and write messages. writer.Complete(); writer.FlushToDisk(); // Optional; omit when only format completion is required. A caller-owned file uses the same two actions: using var stream = new FileStream(path, FileMode.CreateNew, FileAccess.Write); using var writer = new McapWriter(stream, leaveOpen: true); // Register channels and write messages. writer.Complete(); writer.FlushToDisk(); Complete() finishes Chunk, Summary, Footer and end magic, then performs ordinary output flushing. Flush() during writing does not complete the format. Neither requests file persistence. FlushToDisk() calls Rust File::sync_all() for path outputs or FileStream.Flush(true) for a directly supplied FileStream. Wrapped FileStreams and other Streams are not unwrapped. Call FlushToDisk() only after successful completion and before disposal. Every valid invocation performs synchronization again. Calling before completion throws InvalidOperationException; after disposal it throws ObjectDisposedException. Unsupported Streams throw NotSupportedException without failing the writer. Actual synchronization failures terminate the writer: completion, synchronization and summary access then fail; disposal and Stream ownership transfer remain available. Stream exceptions retain their original type and instance. Previously opened independent summary cursors remain usable. The path file handle stays open after completion until disposal. leaveOpen and IntoInner() control Stream ownership as usual. Neither disposal nor ownership transfer implicitly completes or synchronizes the recording. Successful synchronization means the operating-system request succeeded; it is not an unconditional guarantee about hardware, filesystem or directory-entry persistence. Writer options Option Default / meaning Compression, ChunkSize, UseChunks Zstd, 1 MiB, true. ChunkSize follows upstream semantics, including zero; null disables the target-size cutoff. Profile, Library Empty profile; null Library selects the official Rust library identifier. EmitSummaryOffsets, EmitStatistics true; independently control summary offsets and statistics. EmitMessageIndexes, EmitChunkIndexes, EmitAttachmentIndexes, EmitMetadataIndexes true; independently control each index type. RepeatChannels, RepeatSchemas null; upstream defaults (true). Control declarations repeated in the summary. CalculateChunkCrcs, CalculateDataSectionCrc, CalculateSummarySectionCrc, CalculateAttachmentCrcs true; independently control CRC computation. CompressionLevel, CompressionThreads null; upstream defaults and algorithm support. Nullable flags use upstream behavior when null. EmitSummaryRecords applies first; explicitly supplied individual switches override it. DisableSeeking defaults to false for seekable output and true for non-seekable output; explicit false on non-seekable output fails. To omit summary records, disable statistics, chunk/attachment/metadata indexes and repeated declarations. Disable summary offsets separately. No chunks means no chunk compression or chunk message indexes, regardless of their requested settings. Long recordings in one file A single file can retain compression and complete indexes without retaining all message payloads. Writer memory includes active chunk/codec storage, declarations and file-level indexes. The upstream writer accumulates a ChunkIndex for every finished chunk even when EmitChunkIndexes=false; that option controls emission, not accumulation. EmitMessageIndexes=false omits per-chunk message indexes, while EmitAttachmentIndexes=false and EmitMetadataIndexes=false stop retaining their respective indexes. Disabling indexes reduces indexed-query capabilities. Reuse declarations instead of continually adding distinct schemas/channels. Choose ChunkSize using recording duration, throughput and random-read latency. Larger chunks reduce chunk-index counts but can increase active storage and the cost of reading/decompressing a chunk. The size is a target, not a memory ceiling. Avoid unnecessary Flush() calls: they finish the active chunk and can increase index counts. Use file or draining Stream output and bound the caller's pending-write queue; a growing MemoryStream retains the recording itself. No automatic segmentation or index spill is performed. Complete() releases the upstream writer after finishing and retains one shared native summary plus the output. It does not build a persistent JSON summary. GetSummary() encodes the response on demand and returns an independent managed result; requesting the whole summary still requires response and result memory proportional to its contents. OpenSummaryRecords() shares the native summary without whole-summary JSON encoding. Independent cursors can retain it after writer disposal. Upstream finish-time summary cloning remains a transient cost. Dispose the writer when summary/persistence/Stream-transfer operations are finished; single-file recording still has file-level index growth, not constant memory. Complete messages and prepared writes WriteMessage(McapMessage) invokes upstream Writer::write, including automatic declarations using supplied IDs. The prepared overload takes McapPreparedChannel, a matching header and payload span, avoiding repeated managed serialization. Preparation snapshots schema bytes and metadata without registering declarations. Prepared descriptors are immutable; convenience calls observe current inputs. McapPreparedSchema, McapPreparedChannelRegistration, McapPreparedMetadata, McapPreparedAttachment and McapPreparedAttachmentStart snapshot reusable control descriptions. Pass them to the corresponding RegisterSchema, RegisterChannel, WriteMetadata, WriteAttachment or StartAttachment overload. Registration returns a non-nullable ID; other operations return void. Only the complete attachment descriptor accepts a separate payload; schema bytes are captured at construction. Prepared complete-message McapPreparedChannel is distinct from explicit channel registration. Warmed preparation reuse, attachment continuation, private records and Flush retain their allocation gates. WriteMetadata(McapMetadata) and WriteAttachment(McapAttachment) accept owned models directly. Complete() finishes the format; GetSummary() copies its result and OpenSummaryRecords() returns a retained McapSummaryRecordReader. IntoInner() releases native state and transfers Stream ownership without implicit completion. Safe writer rejections McapWriterOptions.SafeRejections is a fixed flags policy captured at construction. By default it enables all five audited pre-mutation rejections: explicit schema registration with ID zero (InvalidSchemaIdOnRegistration), explicit schema conflicts (ConflictingSchemaOnRegistration), either channel registration referencing an unknown schema (UnknownSchemaOnChannelRegistration), explicit channel conflicts (ConflictingChannelOnRegistration), and header/payload writes referencing an unknown channel (UnknownChannelOnMessageWrite). Prepared schema/channel registration follows the same policy. Choose any subset; unknown bits are rejected before file creation or Stream ownership acquisition. A rejected call still throws McapException. CanContinueWriting is true only when this writer was usable after that rejection; correct the input before retrying. It is not a guarantee about subsequent operations or concurrent callers. Full-message writes with automatic declarations, attachment length errors, ID exhaustion, I/O, callbacks, compression failures and panics remain terminal. The library does not retry automatically. Managed argument/state checks retain their existing behavior. To make every native writer failure terminal, configure: var options = new McapWriterOptions { SafeRejections = McapWriterSafeRejections.None }; Successful message writes retain the zero-managed-allocation contract; error handling is outside that contract. Read messages into reusable buffers A McapReaderFactory owns no resources and does not open the file at construction. OpenMessages, OpenRecords and OpenLinear create independent disposable McapMessageReader, McapChunkFlattener and McapLinearReader instances respectively. Each reader owns one advancing native session. Dispose readers or use using. using var session = new McapReaderFactory(path).OpenMessages(new() { Topic = "/sample" }); byte[] buffer = new byte[64 * 1024]; while (true) { var status = session.ReadNext(buffer, out var header, out var length); if (status == McapReadStatus.EndOfStream) break; if (status == McapReadStatus.BufferTooSmall) { buffer = new byte[checked((int)length)]; // caller-chosen growth, outside zero-allocation contract continue; } // Process buffer.AsSpan(0, checked((int)length)) before reusing it. } BufferTooSmall returns the required payload length and message header, leaves the destination untouched and keeps the same record pending. Successful empty messages return Success with length zero. McapReadStatus.Success means an operation produced a result or event; inspect the opcode or event kind to determine its content. EOF is repeatable. Errors terminate message/record advancement. Caller-buffer methods expose no native addresses; separate borrowed methods follow the lifecycle contract below. Filters accept one exact Topic or a Topics collection and apply [StartTime, EndTime) to LogTime. Null boundaries are unbounded; reversed boundaries throw and equal boundaries select nothing. Sequential filtering preserves file order; explicit query execution controls time ordering as described below. Seekable time-ordered queries use the official IndexedReader when summary declarations and chunk coverage suffice and there are no top-level messages. Non-default linear parser flags force high-level queries to scan; indexed-only options do not expose those flags. Missing summary/declarations/statistics, insufficient chunk coverage, top-level messages or a non-seekable source can prevent indexed selection. Missing per-message indexes alone does not prevent it: selected chunks can be parsed for messages. Malformed indexes and parsing/I/O errors can fail instead of falling back. Direct Sans-I/O indexed readers never use scan-and-sort fallback. Choosing a query path Choose execution explicitly; null and empty options are equivalent within each capability. Entry Options and default Execution OpenMessages / ReadMessages McapMessageFilter; file order Sequential scan, including when topic/time filters are supplied OpenIndexedMessages McapIndexedQuery; ascending log time Requires usable indexes; never scans or sorts as fallback QueryMessages / ReadQueryMessages McapQuery; ascending log time Uses indexes where supported, otherwise follows explicit buffered-sort policy StartTime is inclusive and EndTime exclusive. Topic and Topics are mutually exclusive; an empty Topics collection selects nothing. Adding a sequential filter never requests sorting or switches validation to indexed scope. Ascending and reverse log-time order leave tie ordering unspecified. Indexed File order still requires usable indexes even with no filters. McapQuery.AllowBufferedSort defaults to true. Without sufficient indexes, time ordering collects matching messages in native memory before returning the reader; there is no automatic disk spill. Set it to false to reject that collection with NotSupportedException. Indexed-only unavailability raises McapException. McapIndexedQuery contains no fallback controls, and its RecordLengthLimit is separate from linear parsing options. See local allowances. Indexed success is not full-file validation. GetChannel, GetSchema and immutable description lookups do not advance reading. Sequential readers expose encountered declarations; indexed and chunk-message readers may also have declarations supplied by their retained summary. Missing IDs are nonterminal. After an advancing read fails, all further reads and lookups reject with InvalidOperationException; disposal takes precedence with ObjectDisposedException. Previously returned copies, descriptions and leases remain valid. Owned records, summaries and raw records File-factory ReadMessages, ReadSchemas, ReadChannels, ReadMetadata and ReadAttachments create independent scans. Stream classification overloads own an incremental session for the enumeration. Classification validates every expanded record but copies only selected records into managed objects; skipped payloads do not create managed result arrays. Reader enumerations consume their existing cursor. Message and record bodies, schema bytes and attachment data are independent mutable arrays. Message enumeration privately caches declarations and copies mutable schema bytes and metadata into each message. GetSummary() returns complete owned statistics, indexes and Schemas / Channels dictionaries, or null if no summary exists. Schemas repeated in the summary appear in Schemas; a channel can also reference a schema found in the data section without adding that schema to the repeated-schema map. Within one summary, channels may share its schema objects. Separate summary calls are independent, including after producer disposal. A writer's finish summary describes its in-memory result even when summary records were disabled. These records use ordinary .NET record equality: arrays and dictionary interfaces do not acquire Rust-style deep content equality. Direct model construction retains supplied references. OpenLinear() reads top-level records, preserving encoded Chunk bodies. OpenRecords() returns a chunk flattener. Both provide ReadNextRecord and owned ReadRecords; the body excludes opcode and eight-byte length prefix. Unknown/private bodies are preserved. McapChunkReader accepts one encoded Chunk body without the outer record header and validates only that local input. ReadNextMessageRecord on message readers returns the 22-byte message header plus payload and shares pending state with other message delivery forms, including empty payloads and buffer retries. Direct reader adapters McapReaderFactory chooses file or Stream construction; copied and mapped construction lives on the corresponding typed reader. Input ownership does not choose a different result capability. Internal engines and mode codes are not public APIs. Managed reader Official counterpart / scope McapLinearReader read::LinearReader; top-level encoded chunks McapChunkReader read::ChunkReader; one encoded chunk body McapChunkFlattener read::ChunkFlattener; expanded records with the binding's high-level validation baseline McapRawMessageReader read::RawMessageStream; headers/payloads without requiring a known message channel McapMessageReader read::MessageStream; resolved messages and existing buffer/callback/batch/lease delivery McapSummaryRecordReader Binding extension over retained Summary records The upstream read module has five reader types plus Summary; the sixth managed reader is explicitly a summary-record extension. Copied constructors take one independent input copy; OpenMapped retains the mapping. Use SkipStartMagic and SkipEndMagic for explicit magic-free parsing. Record-only types expose no message operations, and raw messages expose no implicit resolved enumeration. All advancing failures are terminal; owned objects and immutable descriptions already returned remain valid. McapRecords.Parse returns IMcapRecord: a typed owned model for each standard record or McapRawRecord for unknown records. Match the concrete result type to access its fields; the interface alone does not imply a known or interpreted record. McapRawRecord explicitly represents an opcode and uninterpreted owned body. McapRecordView.Parse validates through official parse_record and views caller-owned managed memory. Validation applies to the bytes at the time of Parse: keep the backing contents unchanged throughout view and field-cursor use, including through other mutable aliases. Scalar properties and the Fields cursor read UTF-8, maps, arrays and binary fields without creating strings/arrays. ToOwned copies explicitly. ReadFooter and GetCompressedDataOffset directly call the upstream helpers. CreateCopiedIndexedReader() copies a seekable source and reads its official summary without moving the random-access source position. McapIndexedReader.CreateCopied(bytes) also accepts caller bytes. The indexed reader owns memory proportional to the file, independently of its original session. It exposes SeekMessage, OpenChunkMessages/ReadChunkMessages, message indexes, indexed metadata/attachments, footer, descriptions and summary. Random operations use the supplied index fields, including lengths and channel-offset maps; they do not replace the index with a summary entry having the same offset. Metadata and attachment reads accept caller-provided indexes even without a summary. Chunk message and message-index reads still require summary declarations. Index fields not used by the corresponding upstream helper do not add validation. Do not mutate an index's map while a call is in progress. OpenChunkMessages(index) returns an independent disposable McapMessageReader that parses lazily and remains valid after indexed-reader disposal, sharing immutable native input and summary without another file copy. Each ReadChunkMessages enumeration owns an independent cursor. Random operations do not move these cursors. Buffer overloads allocate no managed memory; metadata/attachment buffers contain record bodies, while message indexes use 18-byte little-endian rows (u16 channel ID, u64 log time, u64 offset). Owned message-index results retain a group for each validated channel index, including empty groups. The row buffer represents entries only; use the owned result when empty group identity matters. Insufficient buffers remain untouched. OpenSummaryRecords() provides a buffer cursor for all summary fields and declarations. Prepared Chunk indexes For repeated random access, construct McapPreparedChunkIndex(index) once and dispose it when finished. Construction snapshots the index fields and channel-offset map, encodes once and parses once with the official Rust implementation. Do not mutate the map during construction; later mutations do not affect the prepared index. Prepared overloads of SeekMessage, OpenChunkMessages, ReadChunkMessages, ReadMessageIndexes and GetCompressedDataOffset avoid repeated index encoding, temporary native scratch and index parsing. Existing index overloads continue to observe current caller fields. The encoder enumerates concrete Dictionary maps without boxing and reads concrete SortedList maps by key/value index; both paths visit only existing entries. Other implementations, including ReadOnlyDictionary and SortedDictionary, use the generic lookup fallback. For repeated calls using sparse high-ID maps behind general IReadOnlyDictionary implementations, prefer a prepared index: the nonprepared encoder may probe the ushort key domain (up to 65,536 lookups per call) to avoid enumerator allocations. Preparation snapshots the map once and avoids that repeated work. The fallback avoids allocating an enumerator, but a supplied map or comparer may allocate during lookup; the library does not control those allocations. Each prepared descriptor retains a managed channel-ID array (2 bytes per channel, excluding the array header) to reconstruct empty owned index groups; native storage retains the full parsed index and encoded cache key. Disposal releases native ownership. The managed ID array remains attached to the descriptor until garbage collection. A prepared index can be shared across indexed readers. Every operation still applies the original file-range and summary requirements; preparation does not validate a particular file. Calls, including SeekMessages batches, and disposal are serialized for each involved descriptor. A borrowed snapshot message callback must not invoke operations on any indexed-reader instance (including Dispose) or use/dispose any prepared index; this prevents reversing the descriptor-before-snapshot lock order. Child cursors remain usable after the prepared index and snapshot are disposed. Message-index helper allocations, cache misses and decompression remain possible; preparation does not guarantee zero total native allocation. McapSansIoLinearReader, McapSansIoSummaryReader and McapSansIoIndexedReader expose separate protocols and event types. Linear events contain Read/Record/End; summary events contain Read/Seek/End; indexed events contain only Message/ReadChunk/End. Summary uses NextEvent(out event) without a destination. Linear and summary SupplyInput(data) respond only to Read; indexed input uses only InsertChunkData(offset, data). McapSeekRequest exposes unsigned AbsolutePosition for Begin and signed RelativeOffset for Current/End; inappropriate accessors throw InvalidOperationException. Only summary reading exposes NotifySeeked, and only indexed reading exposes InsertChunkData and SetRecordLengthLimit. A completed summary parser supplies GetSummary, OpenSummaryRecords and CreateIndexed with McapIndexedQuery. Output is copied into caller spans; no native pointer escapes. The binding exposes no custom decompressor registration because upstream provides no registration entry point. Built-in Lz4/Zstd remains upstream-owned. Complete-chunk random access Cache keys use complete caller-supplied index semantics; map insertion order does not change identity. Hits do not decompress again. Uncompressed mapped payloads reference mapping ranges; compressed payloads share decompressed storage. Insufficient-buffer retries retain shared slices. SeekMessages(ReadOnlySpan<McapMessageSeekRequest>) groups requests by chunk within that call, loads each different chunk once, and returns a batch in request order including duplicates. Failure delivers no partial batch. SeekMessage(preparedIndex, entry, visitor) provides borrowed delivery; its callback must not use or dispose any indexed-reader instance or prepared chunk index; buffer and owned-result APIs copy at final delivery. GetCacheStatistics reports hits and chunk loads. Choose the reuse scope that matches the access pattern: Access pattern Method Reuse scope One isolated message SeekMessage Loads the complete target chunk on a cache miss; leaving caching disabled avoids cache retention Many messages in one chunk OpenChunkMessages Traverse one cursor once; reopening a cursor starts a new traversal Known set of discrete requests SeekMessages Groups loads within one call, even with caching disabled; another call is a separate batch Repeated visits across calls Reuse an indexed reader with MaxRandomAccessCacheBytes Retains recent chunks until eviction or indexed-reader disposal The working set is the chunks revisited between cache reuses. Size the allowance for their decompressed storage and descriptors, not compressed file bytes. A working set larger than the allowance can cause eviction and repeated decompression; this remains a valid access pattern. Inspect GetCacheStatistics() hits and chunk loads to assess reuse. Prepared indexes avoid repeated descriptor encoding/parsing, not cache-miss decompression. Copying a returned payload does not cache its source chunk. Random reads validate the complete target chunk and may report tail corruption earlier than prefix reads. This is not full-file validation. See local patches for patch boundaries and evidence. Stream sessions and ownership Use McapReaderFactory.OpenMessages(stream, filter, leaveOpen) or OpenRecords(stream, leaveOpen: leaveOpen) for Stream input. The current stream position is MCAP offset zero. Sessions consume streams incrementally without a whole-stream copy or temporary file. A stream must contain exactly one MCAP from that position to its end. Only one MCAP session can own a Stream at a time. Do not reposition, truncate, read, write or dispose it externally while the session is active. Stream callbacks run synchronously on the initiating thread; reentry into the same writer/session is rejected. Callback exceptions propagate after leaving native code. leaveOpen defaults to false; disposing a session closes its stream unless true. Explicit disposal reports owned Stream and native release failures. Cleanup is attempted once; later Dispose calls do not retry it. Stream exclusion ends only after successful release or ownership transfer. A failed owned Stream release keeps that Stream unavailable for another MCAP session. IntoInner returns the Stream only after native state has been released successfully; it neither completes the format nor disposes the transferred Stream. Finalization is a nonthrowing fallback, not the explicit-disposal error policy. Use OpenRecordAccessor for McapRecordAccessor: it preserves the seekable source position and supports raw-record/chunk/index reads, summary access and independent snapshot creation without first copying the whole input. Its parsing or I/O failures terminate that random-access reader. Sequential readers keep their own failure boundary. Argument checks before an operation, missing declaration lookups and buffer negotiation are nonterminal. If an operation and restoration both fail, both errors are reported. Repeat work through a new reader after safe release. OpenRecordAccessor requires seekable input and rejects non-seekable Streams before taking ownership. McapReaderFactory.GetSummary(stream) uses random access when possible and otherwise scans to EOF. Changing capability requires a new reader; no session-reset protocol is provided. Explicitly copied/mapped readers have no managed Stream to return from IntoInner; Stream-backed readers preserve ownership transfer. Mapped files must remain unchanged across reads, validation and recovery. Windows denies ordinary concurrent write/delete opens while mapped; pre-existing writable mappings are not covered. Linux does not enforce this exclusion. Concurrent truncation of a mapped file can terminate the process. Asynchronous records and errors McapAsyncRecordReader.ReadNextRecordAsync returns ValueTask<McapRecordReadResult>; McapAsyncMessageReader.ReadBatchLeaseAsync returns retained messages without query sorting. Capability is fixed at construction. Both use official Sans-I/O with .NET asynchronous Stream I/O, without hosting Tokio. Expanded record bodies and declaration references are validated before delivery or buffer negotiation, independently of CRC switches. Encountered immutable schema/channel descriptions are available after consuming the outstanding operation. Top-level record delivery has no visibility inside chunks; direct Sans-I/O is raw. Async EOF does not report full-file validation. Allow one outstanding operation and consume each ValueTask exactly once before another operation, lookup, transfer or disposal. Cancellation and I/O/parser errors are terminal. leaveOpen, Stream exclusion and ownership transfer match synchronous reading. DisposeAsync is synchronous release: it calls owned Stream.Dispose and returns a completed ValueTask. It does not wait for pending work or invoke Stream.DisposeAsync; finish and consume the operation first. The reusable completion source and cached continuation provide a warmed 0 B managed-allocation path even when I/O suspends. The gate measures both calling and dedicated I/O threads, including a direct-await loop. Completion may resume the consumer inline on the I/O thread; the library does not force a ThreadPool dispatch. Arbitrary Streams, consumer await machinery, initialization, errors, buffer growth and owned results are excluded. Native allocations are not constrained by this guarantee. McapException.Kind identifies every upstream McapError variant; Details retains its structured fields. Wrapper-only failures use Binding. Original Stream exceptions remain preserved. Native error text is bounded: messages retain up to 256 UTF-8 bytes and textual detail values up to 128, ending at character boundaries. Shortened values carry [truncated]; object details also set truncated: true. Numeric fields remain exact. Native OS errors report osCode and a fixed message instead of allocating localized OS text. Parse errors retain the root cause text rather than the parser’s decorated backtrace. Borrowing, batches and leases Owned results remain independent: McapMessage.Data is a byte[] copy and mutable declarations are defensively copied. ReadNext(McapMessageVisitor) and VisitMessages(visitor, maxMessages) receive an in McapMessageHeader and ReadOnlySpan<byte> without final delivery copying. Return false to stop normally after the current message. Spans expire on callback return. Reading, seeking, inspecting state or disposing the originating reader inside its callback is prohibited; writing to another writer is supported. Callback exceptions are rethrown after normal ABI return. Indexed-reader callbacks additionally prohibit operations on any indexed-reader instance or prepared chunk index, as described under prepared Chunk indexes. GetChannelDescription returns an immutable declaration snapshot shared by subsequent lookups. WriteBatch(headers, payloadStorage, ranges) synchronously consumes contiguous shared storage with one lock and one ABI call. Counts, ranges and all Channels are checked before writing. Return value is the completed count; McapBatchWriteException.CompletedCount excludes the failing record, which may already be partly written. Batches are not atomic. Existing audited safe-rejection settings apply; I/O, compression and post-advancement failures terminate the writer. Input buffers may be reused after return. WriteBatch(batchLease) writes the lease's original headers and payloads. WriteBatch(batchLease, headers) replaces the complete header of each message; the header count must equal batchLease.Count. Register destination schemas/channels first and supply replacement ChannelIds when remapping; no declarations or mappings are inferred. Both overloads use one writer lock and one ABI call, reference payloads across multiple storage owners without concatenating them, and retain the lease handle for the synchronous call. They do not transfer ownership or alter the lease. Do not dispose the lease concurrently with writing. Null/disposed leases and mismatched header counts are rejected before native writing without failing the writer. Channel preflight, safe rejections and completed-prefix failures follow the same batch contract above. Both overloads have a warmed zero-managed-allocation gate; allocating the input lease is a separate cost. ReadBatch(headers, ranges, payloadStorage) fills caller-owned buffers with whole messages and returns count, used bytes, stop reason and the next required capacity. If a later record fails, the call throws and the session becomes terminal; buffers may contain an already written prefix, but no prefix count is returned, so discard the entire call's output. Visitor callbacks that already ran are not rolled back. A failing lease read publishes no partial batch; leases returned by earlier calls remain valid. It preserves the next message when space is insufficient. Borrowed, caller-buffer batch and batch-write paths have warmed Release zero-managed-allocation gates. ReadBatchLease returns McapMessageBatchLease, by default up to 256 messages and a soft 4 MiB payload target. The target is checked after adding a whole message, so a batch may exceed it, including when a single message exceeds the target. GetHeader, GetPayload, CopyTo and RetainMessage(index) access or retain messages without per-message payload arrays. Batches may reference multiple chunks without repacking. Leases remain valid across reader advancement, reader disposal and cache eviction; Dispose is idempotent, with private SafeHandle finalization fallback. Dispose retained message leases separately. Keep a lease in a using scope throughout span use. Access methods reject disposed owners, but an existing span cannot be revoked. Keep the owner alive and never overlap span access with concurrent disposal. Cross-thread transfer is supported with caller synchronization. Mapped files must remain unchanged until every reader, child cursor and lease referencing them is released. ReadBatchLease returns a batch or null at EOF. McapAsyncMessageReader.ReadBatchLeaseAsync awaits I/O and supports cancellation; consume its ValueTask before another operation, lookup or disposal. Cancellation terminates the reader, while delivered leases remain valid. Record and message capabilities use separate types. Both asynchronous expanded readers expose encountered immutable channel/schema descriptions, including unreferenced schemas. Unknown IDs are nonterminal; failed and disposed readers reject lookup. Descriptions survive disposal. Message readers reject EmitChunks. No prefetch queue, spill file or automatic file segmentation is created. Async lease reading uses a reusable completion source and continuation. Each delivered batch may allocate its lease and SafeHandle objects; I/O suspension does not require another per-operation async state machine. A nonempty batch is returned when the parser next requests input, even below the message/payload target. This avoids waiting for extra I/O merely to fill a batch. Stream implementations may have their own allocations. Input completion is consumed before cancellation can release parser resources. Structured error details Unsupported platforms throw PlatformNotSupportedException; native loading errors retain their .NET type. Native operation/ABI failures throw McapException (an IOException). Managed parameter/state checks use standard exceptions, and disposed objects throw ObjectDisposedException. See ABI details and allocation acceptance. McapException.Kind and documented Details field names/types are stable contracts; future versions may add fields and error kinds. Ignore unknown fields and provide a default error-kind branch. Text, including Message and the source/name/description fields, is diagnostic and may be truncated or reworded; do not branch on exact text or infer retry permission from it. Use CanContinueWriting only for the documented writer rejection contract. Kind Details object fields AttachmentTooLarge excess, attachment_length: unsigned numbers AttachmentIncomplete current, expected: unsigned numbers BadAttachmentCrc, BadChunkCrc, BadDataCrc, BadSummaryCrc saved, calculated: unsigned numbers BadAttachmentLength, BadChunkLength, BadSchemaLength header, available: unsigned numbers PrivateRecordOpcodeIsReserved opcode: unsigned number ConflictingChannels, ConflictingSchemas name: string UnknownChannel sequence, channel_id: unsigned numbers UnknownSchema name: string; schema_id: unsigned number UnsupportedCompression compression: string DecompressionError description: string ChunkBufferTooLarge, ChunkTooLarge length: unsigned number RecordTooLarge opcode, len: unsigned numbers BadChunkStartOffset offset: unsigned number Parse, Io source: string; when a native OS code exists, osCode: signed number and fixed source text Binding wrapping a native OS error source: fixed string; osCode: signed number Binding for a local allowance resource: string; limit, requested: unsigned numbers Binding for operation plus position-restoration failure code: "operationRestore"; operation, cleanup: nested error objects containing kind, message, details Other upstream kinds Empty object unless truncation adds a flag Native errors without structured details use JSON null. Message-only managed construction leaves Details Undefined. Any object may additionally carry truncated: true; absent means no truncation was reported. Message text is limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes, textual detail values to 128, including [truncated]. Numeric fields remain exact. Original managed Stream exceptions may bypass McapException entirely. Ordinary records retain .NET array/collection equality, and IReadOnlyDictionary is not a promise of deep immutability; use declaration descriptions for immutable sharing. Validation and recovery File length is not used as a record or decompressed-chunk size limit. Highly compressed chunks can expand beyond the file size; native memory and upstream parser limits still apply. McapReaderFactory.Validate() scans the whole file and checks record parsing, present Chunk/Attachment/Data/Summary CRCs, framing and final magic. Expanded validation rejects invalid/conflicting declaration IDs, channels referencing undeclared nonzero schemas, and messages referencing undeclared channels. It returns a scan record count, not a message count. CRC zero means no checksum was supplied; payload schema semantics are not checked. McapReaderOptions controls magic, trailing bytes, chunk emission, CRC checks and record-length limits. Optional CRC and trailing-byte checks default to false. High-level expanded record and resolved-message reads always parse bodies and validate declaration IDs, conflicts and references, independent of Strict or any individual CRC flag. This baseline applies to Stream, copied, mapped and asynchronous input. Top-level readers do not validate hidden chunk declarations; chunk-local and raw-message readers have explicit narrower scopes. Raw-message reads collect declarations but allow an unknown message channel. Direct Sans-I/O linear events remain raw. The strict preset adds named integrity checks; it does not switch declaration validation on or off. EmitChunks belongs to top-level or raw protocol reading; a chunk flattener rejects it. IsScanComplete reports EOF without an integrity claim. IsFullyValidated and ValidateRemaining require a strict complete expanded scan; indexed, buffered-sort and local-chunk results are insufficient. Description lookup does not count a summary declaration as encountered in a sequential scan. Validation retains distinct schema bodies and channel descriptions to check conflicts; memory grows with declaration bytes and metadata, not just the bounded 16-bit ID domain. Indexed-reader cache controls belong to McapIndexedReaderOptions, not parser options. Validation capability at creation ValidationCapability on message readers and chunk flatteners is fixed at creation and remains readable after failure or disposal. It describes scope, not success: Capability Meaning ValidateRemaining / message recovery PartialInput Indexed, buffered-sort or chunk-local results Rejected before further consumption FullScan Expanded sequential scan without the complete strict configuration Rejected before further consumption StrictFullScan Expanded sequential scan performing strict checks from its start Supported while the session remains usable Sequential topic/time filtering does not remove validation of skipped records. Capability rejection performs no additional I/O, preserves pending buffer retries and does not fault a usable reader. Disposed and failed sessions still reject operations. ValidateRemaining completes checks already active from creation; it cannot retroactively validate skipped checks. RecoverMessages continues the current cursor and counts only matching messages delivered by that invocation. Query construction may already scan and sort before returning; its result is still PartialInput. Prefer factory Validate() and RecoverMessages() when a dedicated complete operation is desired. RecoverMessages(accept) on a strict message reader delivers the valid prefix and retains the original structured parse error in its result. Factory overloads open a strict file-order reader automatically. Use sequential reading for prefix salvage; an explicit sorted query may fail during construction before any prefix can be delivered. Check IsFullyValidated and Error; delivered messages alone prove no integrity. Stream, native I/O, binding and callback exceptions propagate rather than becoming salvage results. Both parsing failure and an accept callback exception terminate the reader; the original callback exception is preserved. Existing returned results survive. Recovery does not permit arbitrary I/O retries or recover bytes never written to the source. Binding performance and local limits After initialization, registration and warm-up, normal WriteToKnownChannel and buffered ReadNext calls are required to allocate exactly zero managed bytes. This hard hot-path contract includes chunk/compression boundaries, newly encountered declarations, insufficient-buffer retries and EOF. This is not zero-copy reading: native data is copied into caller memory. It is not a promise that the process never collects or that Rust never allocates. Buffer growth, owned-record enumeration, description access, startup and errors are outside the guarantee. Arbitrary user Stream implementations can allocate internally; the guarantee covers the library's bridge, not those implementations. Performance contracts concern binding-added allocations and payload copies, not allocations inside the official parser, writer or codecs. Borrowed callbacks and leases reference stable storage; caller-buffer reads copy to the caller, and convenience APIs return independent owned results. Copied constructors own an input copy; OpenMapped shares a mapping and Stream supports incremental input. Setup, descriptors, lease control objects and errors may allocate. Synchronous and asynchronous input reserve the parser's current complete requirement independently of the I/O transfer size, avoiding repeated expansion during short reads. This is not whole-source prebuffering or a total-memory bound. A retained slice can keep a complete chunk or mapping alive; limit outstanding work according to storage size as well as batch count. Cache allowances and batch payload targets do not account for every externally retained byte. Control Counted quantity and default Boundary behavior and exclusions McapQuery.MaxBufferedSortBytes Sum of selected messages' logical payload lengths plus allocated descriptor-array capacity in bytes; null means no collection allowance Exceeding the allowance fails fallback construction/reading, without spilling or partial sorted results. Each selected range counts its length even if backing is shared. Excludes backing amplification, temporary compaction overlap, parser/codec memory and RSS; does not apply to indexed-reader chunk buffering. McapIndexedReaderOptions.MaxRandomAccessCacheBytes Local LRU charge for retained chunk storage, descriptors, keys and index bytes; 0 disables retention Oversized entries load without cache retention. Eviction releases cache references, not caller leases. Excludes allocator overhead, parsing temporaries, snapshot input and externally retained owners. Uncompressed mapped chunks are charged their logical decompressed size. ReadBatchLease count and payload target Default maximum 256 messages; soft target 4 MiB of logical payload Checks the byte target after each whole message, so it can overshoot. Does not limit backing capacity or all outstanding batches. Async batches may return earlier at an input request. Indexed-reader cache controls belong to McapIndexedReaderOptions. McapIndexedQuery has no buffered fallback settings; McapQuery.AllowBufferedSort=false rejects fallback collection entirely. RecordLengthLimit controls linear record bodies; indexed construction also checks compressed and decompressed chunk sizes, and later indexed reads check their relevant record lengths. Changing the Sans-I/O indexed limit does not repeat construction-time checks. Summary limits apply to summary record bodies and may be tightened by known source size. None of these local controls is a process-wide memory limit. Choosing storage for retained results Choose borrowing, sharing or independent copies by retention duration; see message ownership for the copy example. The following rules define backing retention and reclamation. A lease retains backing ownership, not just its visible payload range. RetainMessage shares that ownership; it does not trim the allocation. A small message can retain a full decompressed chunk, a complete copied input or a file mapping. A batch may retain several owners, and several batches may share one owner. Disposal releases that owner's reference; storage can be reclaimed only after all references are released. Other leases, parsers, snapshots, child cursors or caches may still retain it. Copying one slice therefore does not guarantee immediate reclamation. A snapshot itself retains its input until it and every dependent owner release it. Mapping size is address space, not a measurement of resident memory. For predictable pipeline retention, bound outstanding work using distinct backing sizes and retention duration as well as batch count. Long-term sharing remains valid when retaining the backing is acceptable; copying sparse results is a performance choice, not a lifetime requirement. Buffered sort chooses storage before publishing results. It groups selected messages by consecutive owned backing, retaining dense groups and compacting sparse groups at an owner change or end of scan. The current internal policy copies when capacity is at least four times selected payload bytes and saves at least 256 KiB of group backing capacity. Compact segments target 256 KiB at message boundaries; larger messages get their own segment. Empty payloads retain no backing. External storage, including mappings, stays shared. These thresholds are implementation choices, not public tuning options or performance guarantees. Compaction preserves message order, retries and lease lifetimes. It copies selected payloads once and temporarily holds old and new storage together. Other owners can delay actual reclamation. Sorting still collects results before delivery; its logical allowance does not cover transient copies, retained backing amplification, parser/codec memory or process RSS. Use the site's API reference (English) for individual parameters and return values; see testing for measurement methods.
